mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar non-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer spending proxies (not available in evidence - thus cannot be used) would typically signal demand weakness, but here we proxy with a sharp decrease in home sales (HOUST) as a leading indicator, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by > 10% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) beyond 2% monthly suggests supply expansion that outpaces demand, leading to valuation compression and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show positive or flat performance during periods of accelerated supply growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, it triggers a forward-looking discounting effect that reduces expected equity returns, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.0% in a month following a sustained decline below 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during prior inflation sub-trends (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 5% without a corresponding rise in wage growth proxies (not available) suggests a tight labor market that can drive inflationary expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with UNRATE (Pearson's rho < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 jobs while the S&P 500 20-day log returns remain flat indicates that labor market strength has not translated into equity market optimism, suggesting a potential for negative forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 200,000 each month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: gradual labor market expansion without equity reaction
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show a positive correlation with PAYEMS growth (Pearson's rho > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained rise in consumer confidence proxies (not available) would typically signal supply disruptions, but here we use a sharp drop in home sales (HOUST) as a leading indicator to predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by > 15% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative compared to the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).
